name: Florida
finding: DBPR verifies electrical contractors and the business they qualify. Match both names to the proposal.
question: Ask the local permit office which site plan, wind anchorage and flood-elevation documents it needs. Do not assume a neighbor’s approved pad is suitable for your property.

name: Texas
finding: TDLR states that non-exempt electrical work must be performed by licensed individuals through a licensed electrical contractor.
question: Ask your serving utility about meter capacity and coordination. Record electrical and fuel-provider responsibilities separately; generator fuel availability is a property-specific question.

name: Louisiana
finding: The state contractor search lists currently licensed or registered contractors and offers classification and parish searches. Confirm classification and local requirements rather than inferring permission from a search match.
question: Ask the parish or municipal authority about floodplain review, siting and inspection sequence. Get restoration and trenching exclusions in writing.

name: North Carolina
finding: NCBEEC provides an active electrical-contractor lookup. Verify the firm and applicable classification.
question: Identify the actual city or county permit authority for the property. Ask which fuel-trade credentials, terrain access and site conditions need separate review.

name: South Carolina
finding: The Residential Builders Commission describes residential electrical and plumbing licensing categories. Check the category applicable to the proposed work.
question: Ask the local authority to identify the correct residential trade approvals, site documentation and final inspections before accepting a single bundled permit allowance.

name: Georgia
finding: The state board licenses electrical contractors, rather than electricians as a general category. Verify the contractor credential behind the bid.
question: Ask which local department handles electrical, fuel and site approvals. Separate tree/access work and utility coordination from generator equipment pricing.

name: New York
finding: The Department of State directs local licensing, zoning and project code questions to the local building department; its code division does not handle electrician licensing.
question: Identify the city, town or village responsible for the property. Do not extrapolate NYC or one Long Island jurisdiction’s process to the rest of the state.

name: New Jersey
finding: Consumer Affairs provides professional and business license verification; electrical contractor businesses use the business search.
question: Ask the local construction office which subcode applications and fuel-trade credentials apply, and who coordinates utility work and final approval.
